# useField

> A validated field: value, touched, dirty, error, async checks and accessible `aria-invalid` / `aria-describedby` props.

🟡 intermediate · React 18.0+ · Custom Hooks › Forms & input · support: universal

**Playground:** `npm run dev` → [`#/entry/use-field`](http://localhost:5173/#/entry/use-field)

## Concept

Owns one text value plus its touched/dirty/error state and decides _when_ to validate (`validateOn: "change" | "blur" | "touched"`). Validation runs through `useFormValidation`, so async validators get stale-result protection.

## Problem

Showing errors at the right time is subtle: on every keystroke is noisy, only on blur leaves stale errors while fixing, and forgetting `aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby` leaves screen-reader users without the message.

## When to use

- A standalone validated input: inline-edit, a search box with rules, a settings field saved on blur.
- Learning the building blocks before reaching for `useForm`.

## When not to use

- Several fields submitted together, cross-field rules or dirty tracking — use `useForm`.
- Rules that the browser already enforces well (`required`, `type="email"`, `pattern`) on a simple form — the native [Constraint Validation API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Guides/Constraint_validation) may be enough.
- Large or highly dynamic forms (dozens of fields, nested arrays, schema validation with Zod/Valibot, field-level re-render isolation): use [React Hook Form](https://react-hook-form.com/), [TanStack Form](https://tanstack.com/form/latest) or [Formik](https://formik.org/docs/overview). These hooks are small and readable on purpose.

## API

```ts
function useField(options?: {
  initialValue?: string;
  validate?: Validator | Validator[];
  validateAsync?: (value: string, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<string | undefined>;
  asyncDebounceMs?: number;
  validateOn?: 'change' | 'blur' | 'touched';
  id?: string;
}): UseFieldResult;
```

| Parameter                    | Type                                      | Description                                                     |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `validate` _(optional)_      | `(value) => string \| undefined \| (…)[]` | Pure sync validators; the first message wins.                   |
| `validateAsync` _(optional)_ | `(value, signal) => Promise<message>`     | Runs only when sync rules pass. Pass `signal` to `fetch`.       |
| `validateOn` _(optional)_    | `'change' \| 'blur' \| 'touched'`         | Default `touched`: first on blur, then on every change.         |
| `id` _(optional)_            | `string`                                  | Input id; defaults to `useId()`. The error id is `${id}-error`. |

**Returns:** `value`, `setValue`, `error`, `touched`, `dirty`, `isValidating`, `validate()`, `reset()`, `errorId` and `inputProps` (`id`, `value`, `onChange`, `onBlur`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`).

## Execution flow

1. Render: derives `dirty` (value ≠ initial) and builds `inputProps`; `aria-describedby` points at `errorId` only while there is an error.
2. Change: the value is written to a ref _and_ state, then validated if the mode says so (`change`, or `touched` after the first blur).
3. Blur: marks the field touched and validates immediately (async debounce skipped).
4. Unmount: pending async validation is aborted by `useFormValidation`.

## Common mistakes

### Error text that is not connected to the input

❌ Incorrect:

```tsx
<input aria-invalid={!!error} />
<span className="error">{error}</span>
```

A screen reader announces "invalid" without saying why. The message must be referenced by `aria-describedby`.

✅ Correct:

```tsx
<input {...field.inputProps} />;
{
  field.error && <p id={field.errorId}>{field.error}</p>;
}
```

### Validating on every keystroke from the first character

❌ Incorrect:

```tsx
useField({ validate: email, validateOn: 'change' });
```

Users see "invalid email" after typing one letter. `touched` waits for the first blur, then gives live feedback while fixing.

## Edge cases

- Changing `validateOn` does not reset `touched`; remount the field (`key`) for a clean start, as the demo does.
- `reset()` cancels a pending async check, so a late "taken" result cannot reappear.

## Browser support

Ids come from `useId`, so they match between server and client.
